title: Quantifying Information Hierarchy for Neutrino Oscillation Parameters at JUNO
authors: Yu-han Shu, Neetu Raj Singh Chundawat, Luis A. Delgadillo, Yu-Feng Li
abstract: Since neutrinos are quantum systems inherently, the precision with which oscillation parameters can be estimated ultimately depends on how much information about these parameters is encoded in the neutrino state and how efficiently that information can be extracted through measurement. In this work, we quantify how information encoded in reactor antineutrino states flows through the measurement process to the events observed at the detector, using quantum and classical Fisher information. We establish the information ladder for JUNO, revealing that the loss of precision across different information levels is strongly parameter dependent. We demonstrate that the JUNO configuration approaches the optimal statistical limit for the oscillation parameters of the solar sector, while information on $θ_{13}$ and $Δm_{31}^{2}$ is significantly degraded by the measurement strategy and detector effects. Despite this information loss, the remaining information is sufficient for JUNO to achieve sub-percent precision on $Δm_{31}^{2}$ within six years.
summary: This work develops an 'information ladder' to quantify how well neutrino oscillation parameters can be measured using reactor antineutrinos at the JUNO experiment. By comparing Quantum, Flavor, and Event-level Fisher Information, the authors show that while some parameters are well-constrained, others suffer significant information loss due to detector limitations. Despite this, the remaining information is sufficient for high-precision measurements.
main_problem: The paper quantifies how information about neutrino oscillation parameters is encoded in the quantum state and how efficiently this information can be extracted through measurement.
main_result: While information on solar parameters approaches the optimal statistical limit, information on $\theta_{13}$ and $\Delta m_{31}^{2}$ is significantly degraded by detector effects, though sufficient for sub-percent precision on $\Delta m_{31}^{2}$ at JUNO.
method: It establishes an 'information ladder' by comparing three levels of Fisher Information: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), classical flavor Fisher information, and event-level Fisher information.
model_or_system: The analysis uses the framework of neutrino oscillations, specifically modeling reactor antineutrino states propagating to the JUNO detector baseline.
key_observables: The relative information retained at different levels ($	ext{e}F_{	ext{flavor}}/	ext{e}F_{	ext{Q}}$ and $F_{	ext{event}}/F_{	ext{Q}}$) and the resulting $1\sigma$ precision for the oscillation parameters.
important_parameters: Oscillation parameters: $\theta_{12}, \theta_{13}, \Delta m_{21}^2, \Delta m_{31}^2$. The analysis is performed for the JUNO setup (20 kton, 52.5 km, 6 years).
main_assumptions: The analysis models energy resolution using a Gaussian function and neglects matter effects in some calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy dependence of the diagonal Fisher-information elements for the four parameters across the three information levels, showing the hierarchy and parameter dependence.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by deriving the QFI matrix elements, compares this to the flavor-FI derived from the survival probability, and finally incorporates detector effects to yield the event-level FI, establishing the information hierarchy.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of quantum information theory (QFI) to particle physics measurements provides a powerful, general framework for assessing experimental limits, which is relevant for any field involving quantum state estimation.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Diagonal Fisher-information elements for JUNO with 3% energy resolution including signal and background contributions, shown for NO. Each subplot corresponds to one oscillation parameter: θ12, θ13, ∆m2 21, and ∆m2 31. The upper panels show the event-weighted QFI eFQ αα, the event-weighted electron flavor-FI eF¯e¯e αα, and the event-level Fisher information Fevent αα as functions of the true antineutrino energy Eν. The lower panels show the corresponding information fractions, eF¯e¯e αα/eFQ αα(blue) and Fevent αα /eFQ αα (purple).

FIG. 2. Relative 1σ precision for the four oscillation parameters in JUNO, comparing diagonal and marginalized constraints for both NO and IO, as well as energy resolutions of 3% and 3.5%. The diagonal values are extracted from the diagonal elements of the Fisher information matrix, while the marginalized values account for correlations via the inverse of the full Fisher matrix. Blue diamond markers indicate the statistics-only precision, whereas star markers denote the full statistics plus systematics projected six-year precision reported by the JUNO Collaboration [26].
FIG. 3. Energy dependence of the single-neutrino QFI matrix elements for an electron antineutrino propagating in vacuum at the JUNO baseline.
